assessment.nobel_worthiness: A theoretical prediction of flat bands at the magic angle, followed by the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene, opened an entire field of moire quantum materials. It is a genuinely new tunable platform for correlated electrons, and a clear case where experiment overturned what theorists expected from a simple carbon system. The combination of quantitative band-structure theory and measurement is exactly the kind of work I value.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum-model prediction and the Jarillo-Herrero group's 2018 experiments are the two decisive pillars, giving a natural theory-plus-experiment pairing. Bistritzer co-authored the key 2011 paper with MacDonald, so omitting him is a real cost, and a three-person prize would also be defensible. Others (e.g. the Cao/Fatemi and Yacoby or Dean groups) contributed but are not in the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups have reproduced the correlated phases and superconductivity, and the theoretical picture has been refined over seven or more years. Recognition is timely and the field is still very active, so the interpretation of the superconducting pairing remains open without undermining the core discovery.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene is not settled.
Whether Bistritzer should be included instead of, or alongside, the experimental credit is unresolved.
I cannot independently verify priority details for earlier moire-band theory or for competing experimental groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Altermagnetism identifies a third class of collinear magnetic order with compensated moments but spin-split bands arising from crystal symmetry. This is a conceptual reclassification of magnetism, grounded in spin-group symmetry and first-principles calculations, with obvious spintronics relevance. It sits in my own area, and the prediction-by-DFT then spectroscopic-confirmation pattern is what I find most convincing.
assessment.attribution: Sinova, Šmejkal and Jungwirth formulated and popularized the classification around 2019-2022, and the same group drove the key early predictions and the spin-split band proposals. Other groups (e.g. Hayami, Yuan, Mazin and collaborators) published related symmetry analyses in parallel, so priority is not entirely clean and a prize committee would need to examine this carefully.
assessment.maturity: Spin-resolved ARPES and related measurements on materials such as MnTe and CrSb support the predicted band splitting, but the field is young and the device-level and thermodynamic consequences are not fully established. A prize now would be somewhat early, but the physics is robust.
uncertainties: Priority relative to parallel symmetry-based work by other groups is partly unresolved.
The strength and number of independent confirmations across several material families is still growing.
I rely on my general knowledge of the recent experiments and have not verified individual results.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Angle-resolved photoemission is the direct probe of band structure, Fermi surfaces, gaps and many-body renormalizations in solids. Its development into a high-resolution tool transformed the study of high-Tc cuprates, topological materials and correlated systems, and it is the experimental counterpart to the electronic-structure theory I work with daily. Its impact on how we compare calculation with measurement is enormous.
assessment.attribution: Campuzano and Shen are most associated with applying high-resolution ARPES to cuprate superconductors, with Johnson contributing to early methodology and spin-resolved work. Instrumentation and technique credit is diffuse, with many other pioneers (including those in earlier photoemission theory and synchrotron instrument development) outside this list, so a clean two- or three-person configuration is debatable.
assessment.maturity: The technique is decades old, widely used and independently validated everywhere. Recognition is clearly not premature, though the Committee must decide whether a technique and its applications constitute a single discovery or invention.
uncertainties: Whether the prize can be framed as one discovery or invention rather than a broad technique.
Credit among many instrument and method contributors is diffuse, and the supplied names may not capture the decisive set.
I am uncertain of precise historical priority details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reproducible large room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions in 1995 turned spin-dependent tunneling into a practical effect, underlying read heads and MRAM. It is a quantum-transport phenomenon with a clear connection to spin-polarized band structure and a direct technological payoff, following the logic of the 2007 GMR prize.
assessment.attribution: Moodera and Miyazaki independently reported the room-temperature effect in 1995, which gives a natural two-person core. Parkin's contribution on optimized and coherent MgO barriers (with Yuasa and others, and the earlier Julliere and theory work by Butler and Mathon outside this list) complicates the picture, so a fair split of credit among 'amorphous barrier' versus 'coherent MgO barrier' discoveries is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: The effect is very well confirmed and technologically deployed for decades, so timing is not premature. Possible overlap with the 2007 GMR recognition may reduce the sense of novelty.
uncertainties: Allocation between the first room-temperature observations and the later MgO coherent-tunneling breakthrough.
Whether the Committee views this as sufficiently distinct from the GMR prize.
Theoretical contributors to coherent tunneling are not in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory gave a controlled, non-perturbative framework for the Mott transition and strongly correlated metals, and combined with DFT it became the standard route to realistic correlated-material spectra. It is a foundational and quantitatively predictive theory that I use and respect, with deep influence across condensed matter.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt introduced the infinite-dimension limit, and Georges and Kotliar established the mapping to the Anderson impurity model and the practical DMFT scheme, with Kotliar later driving DFT+DMFT. Metzner is not on the credited list, which makes the proposed set an incomplete picture of the originators. Georges, Kotliar and Vollhardt are the most defensible available trio.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of use, benchmarking against experiment, and extensions make this mature. A theory prize is harder to justify when the decisive confirmation is spread across many materials, and the approximations in DFT+DMFT remain debated.
uncertainties: Omission of Metzner and other early contributors from the credited names.
The Committee has historically been cautious about computational and method-based theory prizes.
Quantitative success of DFT+DMFT is still material-dependent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall state and topological insulators, and its experimental realization in HgTe quantum wells, established a new class of electronic matter with protected edge or surface states. It followed naturally from the topological ideas honored in 2016 and has influenced materials discovery broadly.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the Z2 classification and the quantum spin Hall prediction in graphene; Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental observation in HgTe following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu, Moore and Balents, plus Hasan's 3D topological insulator photoemission, are outside this trio or contested, so the fair split of credit is a significant open question.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by many groups in both 2D and 3D, and materials predictions agree well with ARPES and transport. Timely, but the large number of deserving contributors complicates a clean award, and it competes with related candidates on the list.
uncertainties: Many deserving theorists and experimentalists cannot all be included in a three-person prize.
Overlap with the related topological-insulator and quantum anomalous Hall entries on the longlist.
Whether the HgTe observation or the 3D photoemission work is considered decisive.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of Nd2Fe14B permanent magnets, independently by Sagawa and Croat in 1983-84, produced the strongest commercial permanent magnets and is central to wind turbines, electric vehicles and electronics. It has high practical importance for sustainable energy, an area I care about, and rests on understanding of rare-earth transition-metal magnetism and anisotropy.
assessment.attribution: Sagawa (sintered magnets, Sumitomo) and Croat (melt-spun, General Motors) discovered the compound independently and near-simultaneously, giving a clean two-person attribution. Subsequent contributors to the structure and microstructure engineering are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Entirely mature and widely commercialized. The main hesitation is that this is primarily a materials invention rather than a new physical principle, so I would want a clear physical discovery at its center.
uncertainties: Whether the Committee regards a materials discovery as sufficiently a physics discovery.
Possible concerns about the weight of industrial development relative to fundamental insight.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics created strong coupling of superconducting qubits to microwave resonators, enabling quantum-nondemonstrative readout, gates and the modern superconducting quantum computing architecture. It shows quantum mechanics producing new behavior in engineered solid-state devices, and fits naturally after the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunneling.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf wrote the foundational 2004 theory and experimental proposal; Wallraff and Schoelkopf's groups did the first experiments. Four credited names exceed the three-person limit, and Blais is plausibly as central as Girvin on the theory side. The proposal of three is therefore a judgment call that depends on weighting theory against experiment.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and now the platform of industrial quantum computers. The 2025 prize already recognized related superconducting circuit physics, so the Committee might judge this premature or too close in theme.
uncertainties: Close thematic overlap with the 2025 prize may weigh against a near-term award.
Allocation among four principal contributors cannot all be honored.
Distinguishing fundamental discovery from enabling engineering is difficult.
